label: alp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\cite[Lemma 2.6]{ylh}\label{alp}
	Let $0<p<\infty$ and $\alpha>-2$.
	A function $f\in AT_p^\infty(\alpha)$ if and only if for each (or some) $t>0$,
	$$
	\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}|f(z)|^p(1-|z|^2)^{\alpha+1}dA(z)<\infty.
	$$
head: environment

label: th3.1
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: le2.5
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: l3.1a
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{l3.1a}
	Let $0<p<\infty$, $\alpha>-1$, $t> \frac{1}{p}$ and $f\in AT_p^\infty(\alpha)$. 
	Then
	\[
	\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}|f(\overline{w}z)|^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z)\lesssim \|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p
	\]
	for all \( w \in \mathbb{D}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let  $1\le p<\infty$, \(\alpha>-1\), \(f \in AT_p^\infty(\alpha)\) and \(g \in A^1\). Then 
	\[
	\|\mathbb{K}_g f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}
	\lesssim \|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}\|g\|_{A^1}.
	\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Using Minkowski's inequality and Lemma \ref{l3.1a}, for $t> \frac{1}{p}$, we obtain
	\begin{align*}
		\|\mathbb{K}_g f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}=&\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\left(\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}|\mathbb{K}_g f(z)|^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z)\right)^\frac{1}{p}\\
		\le &\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\left(\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}\left(\int_{\mathbb{D}}|f(\overline{w}z)||g(w)|dA(w) \right)^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z)\right)^\frac{1}{p}\\
		\le &\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}|g(w)|\left( \int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}|f(\overline{w}z)|^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z) \right)^\frac{1}{p}dA(w)\\
		\lesssim&
		\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}\int_{\mathbb{D}}|g(w)|dA(w)\\
		 \lesssim&\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}\|g\|_{A^1}.
	\end{align*}
	The proof is complete.
head: environment

label: az
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: re2a
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{re2a}
From Lemma \ref{az}, if $K$ is a compact subset of $\mathbb{D}$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that
$$
|f(z)|\leq C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}~~ {\text and}~~
|f'(z)|\leq C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}
$$
for all $z\in K$.
head: environment

label: le2a
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{le2a}
Let $0<p<\infty$, $\alpha>-2$, and $f\in AT_p^\infty(\alpha)$. Then
$$
\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}\left|\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|f(z-s)||ds|\right|^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z)\le C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p
$$
for any $t>0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $z=re^{i\theta}$ and $s=\rho e^{i\theta}$, $0\le \rho \le \frac{r}{2}$. Then,
\[
\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|f(z - s)||ds|=\int_{\frac{r}{2}}^{r}|f(\rho e^{i\theta})|d\rho\leq\int_{0}^{r}|f(\rho e^{i\theta})|d\rho.
\]
Applying Lemma \ref{az}, we deduce that
\begin{align*}
	\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|f(z - s)||ds|
	\leq&\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}\int_{0}^{r}\frac{d\rho}{(1-\rho)^{\frac{\alpha+2}{p}}}\\
\le&  \begin{cases} 
	\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)} \left( \frac{1 - (1 - r)^{1-\frac{\alpha+2}{p}}}{1-\frac{\alpha+2}{p}  } \right), & 1-\frac{\alpha+2}{p} \neq 0 \\
	\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)} |\ln(1 - r)| ,& 1-\frac{\alpha+2}{p} = 0.
\end{cases}
\end{align*}
Hence, when $1-\frac{\alpha+2}{p} \neq 0$, for any $t>0$, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}\left|\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|f(z-s)||ds|\right|^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z)\\
\leq &C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p
\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}(1-|z|^2)^{p-1}dA(z)\\
\leq& C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p.
\end{aligned}
\]
When $1-\frac{\alpha+2}{p}=0$, for any $t>0$, we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
	&\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}\left|\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|f(z-s)||ds|\right|^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z)\\
	\le& C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}|\ln(1-|z|^2)|^{p}dA(z)\\
	\le& C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p,
\end{aligned}
\]
as desired. The proof is complete.
head: environment

label: a1.1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{a1.1}
Let $1\le p<\infty$ and $\alpha>-2$. The Hardy-Carleson type tent space \(AT_p^\infty(\alpha)\) is a unital (the unit here is the constant function \(1\)) commutative Banach algebra with respect to Duhamel product \(\circledast\). Denote the algebras as \((AT_p^\infty(\alpha),\circledast)\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $f,g\in AT^\infty_p(\alpha)$.
Using $(\ref{'})$ and Remark \ref{re2a}, we get
\[
\begin{aligned}
	|(f \circledast g)(z)|\leq
	&C\|g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|f(z - s)||ds|+C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|g(z-s)||ds|\\
	&+C\|g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}|f(z)|+C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}|g(z)|+C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}\|g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
When \(1\le p<\infty\), using Lemma \ref{alp} and Minkowski’s inequality, for any $t>0$, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\|(f \circledast g)\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p\\
=&\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}| (f \circledast g)(z) |^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z)\\
\leq&
C\|g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}\left|\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|f(z-s)||ds|\right|^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z)\\
&+C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}\left|\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|g(z-s)||ds|\right|^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z)\\
&+C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p\|g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p.
\end{aligned}
\]
Applying Lemma \ref{le2a}, we have
\[
\|(f \circledast g)\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}\leq C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)} \|g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}.
\]
The proof is complete.
head: environment

title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(f\in AT_q^\infty(\beta) \) and \(g\in AT_p^\infty(\alpha) \). Using  $(\ref{'})$ and Remark \ref{re2a}, we get
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		|(f \circledast g)(z)|\leq
		&C\|g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|f(z - s)||ds|+C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|g(z-s)||ds|\\
		&+C\|g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}|f(z)|+C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}|g(z)|+C\|f\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}\|g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	Using Lemma \ref{az}, we obtain
	\begin{align*}
		 \int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|f(z - s)||ds|
		\leq&\|f\|_{AT_q^\infty(\beta)}\int_{0}^{r}\frac{d\rho}{(1-\rho)^{\frac{\beta+2}{q}}}\\
		\le&  \begin{cases} 
			\|f\|_{AT_q^\infty(\beta)} \left( \frac{1 - (1 - r)^{1-\frac{\beta+2}{q}}}{1-\frac{\beta+2}{q}  } \right), & 1-\frac{\beta+2}{q} \neq 0, \\
			\|f\|_{AT_q^\infty(\beta)} |\ln(1 - r)| ,& 1-\frac{\beta+2}{q} = 0.
		\end{cases}
	\end{align*}
	Therefore, when $1-\frac{\beta+2}{q} \neq 0$ and $p\left(1-\frac{\beta+2}{q} \right)+\alpha+1>-1$, for any $t>0$, by Lemma \ref{alp} or Lemma 3.10 in \cite{z1} we have
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		&\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}\left|\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|f(z-s)||ds|\right|^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z)\\
		\leq&C\|f\|_{AT_q^\infty(\beta)}^p
		\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}(1-|z|^2)^{p\left(1-\frac{\beta+2}{q} \right)+\alpha+1}dA(z)\\
		\leq& C\|f\|_{AT_q^\infty(\beta)}^p. 
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	When $1-\frac{\beta+2}{q}=0$, for any $t>0$, we get
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		&\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}\left|\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|f(z-s)||ds|\right|^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z)\\
		\le& C\|f\|_{AT_q^\infty(\beta)}^p\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}|\ln(1-|z|^2)|^{p}dA(z)\\
		\le& C\|f\|_{AT_q^\infty(\beta)}^p.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	Repeating the steps of the proof of Theorem \ref{a1.1}, for any $t>0$, we deduce that
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		\|\mathfrak{D}_{f}g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p
		\leq&C\|g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}\left|\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|f(z-s)||ds|\right|^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z)\\
		&+C\|f\|_{AT_q^\infty(\beta)}^p\sup_{a\in\mathbb{D}}\int_{\mathbb{D}}\frac{(1-|a|^2)^t}{|1-\overline{a}z|^{t+1}}\left|\int_{0}^{\frac{z}{2}}|g(z-s)||ds|\right|^{p}(1-|z|^{2})^{\alpha+1}dA(z)\\
		&+C\|f\|_{AT_q^\infty(\beta)}^p\|g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p.
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	Applying Lemma \ref{le2a}, it follows  that 
	\[
	\|\mathfrak{D}_{f}g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}\leq C\|f\|_{AT_q^\infty(\beta)}\|g\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}.
	\]

label: at
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{at}
Let $0<p<\infty$ and $\alpha>-2$.
Then $g\in AT_p^\infty(\alpha)$ if and only if 
$$
\sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}}  \int_{\mathbb{D}} |g'(w)|^p (1 - |w|^2)^{p+\alpha} (1 - |\varphi_b(w)|^2) dA(w)<\infty.
$$

label: com
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{com}	Let $0<p<\infty$ and $\alpha>-2$.	Let \(T : AT_p^\infty(\alpha) \to AT_p^\infty(\alpha)\) be a bounded linear operator. Then \(T \) is compact if and only if for any bounded sequence \(\{f_j\}\) in \(AT_p^\infty(\alpha)\) which converges to zero uniformly on compact subsets of \(\mathbb{D}\),                                                                     
	\[\lim _{j \to \infty}\left\|Tf_{j}\right\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}=0.\]
head: environment

label: cmub
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{cmub}
Let \(1 \leq p<\infty\) and \(\alpha>-2\). Let \(\mu\) be a finite positive Borel measure on $[0, 1)$. The Ces\`aro-like operator \(\mathcal{C}_\mu\) is bounded on \(AT_p^\infty(\alpha)\) if and only if \(\mu\) is a Carleson measure.
head: environment

label: xy
title: Proof
body_md:
First we assume that \(\mathcal{C}_\mu\) is bounded on \(AT_p^\infty(\alpha)\). For $0<\rho<1$,  let 
\[f_{\rho}(z)=\frac{(1-\rho)}{(1-\rho z)^{ \frac{\alpha+2}{p}+1}}, \quad z\in \mathbb{D}.\]
After calculation, we see that \(f_{\rho} \in AT_p^\infty(\alpha)\) and \(\sup _{0<\rho<1}\left\|f_{\rho}\right\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)} \lesssim 1\). This implies that \(\mathcal{C}_\mu(f_{\rho}) \in AT_p^\infty(\alpha)\).
Using Lemma \ref{az}, we have 
\[
\left|\mathcal{C}_{\mu}\left(f_{\rho}\right)(\rho)\right| \lesssim \frac{1}{(1-\rho)^{ \frac{\alpha+2}{p}}},\quad 0<\rho<1.
\]
Then, for \(\frac{1}{2}<\rho<1\), 
\[\begin{aligned} 
\frac{1}{(1-\rho)^{ \frac{\alpha+2}{p}}} & \gtrsim\left|\int_{0}^{1} \frac{(1-\rho)}{(1-t \rho)\left(1-t \rho^{2}\right)^{ \frac{\alpha+2}{p}+1}} d \mu(t)\right| \\ 
& \gtrsim \int_{\rho}^{1} \frac{(1-\rho)}{(1-t \rho)\left(1-t \rho^{2}\right)^{ \frac{\alpha+2}{p}+1}} d \mu(t)   \gtrsim \frac{\mu([\rho, 1))}{(1-\rho)^{ \frac{\alpha+2}{p}+1}},
\end{aligned}\]
which implies that $\mu([\rho, 1)) \lesssim 1-\rho $
for all $\frac{1}{2}<\rho<1$.  Hence, \(\mu\) is a Carleson measure.
	
Conversely, assume that \(\mu\) is a Carleson measure.
Let $f\in AT_p^\infty(\alpha)$.
Without loss of generality, we may assume \(f(0)=0\). By Lemma \ref{az},
we get 
   
                                                                               
   
           
   
                                                                                             
   
                        
                                                            
\[\begin{aligned} 
 \left|\mathcal{C}_{\mu}(f)'(z)\right|  
=&\left|\int_{0}^{1} \frac{t f'(t z)}{1-t z}+\frac{t f(t z)}{(1-t z)^{2}} d \mu(t)\right| \\ 
\leq &\int_{0}^{1} \frac{\left|t f'(t z)\right|}{|1-t z|} d \mu(t)+\int_{0}^{1} \frac{|t f(t z)|}{|1-t z|^{2}} d \mu(t) \\ 
\lesssim& \| f\| _{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}\left( \int_{0}^{1} \frac{d \mu(t)}{|1-t z|(1-t|z|)^{ \frac{\alpha+2}{p}+1}}+ \int_{0}^{1} \frac{d \mu(t)}{|1-t z|^{2}(1-t|z|)^{ \frac{\alpha+2}{p}}}\right) \\ 
\lesssim&\| f\| _{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)} \int_{0}^{1} \frac{d \mu(t)}{|1-t z|(1-t|z|)^{ \frac{\alpha+2}{p}+1}}. 
\end{aligned}\]
Using Lemma \ref{at} and Minkowski’s inequality, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\| \mathcal{C}_\mu (f) \|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p  
\asymp  \sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}}  \int_{\mathbb{D}} |\mathcal{C}_\mu (f)'(z)|^p (1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha} (1 - |\varphi_b(z)|^2) dA(z)  \\
\lesssim& \| f \|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p \sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}} (1 - |b|^2)  \int_{\mathbb{D}} \left( \int_0^1 \frac{d\mu(t)}{|1 - tz|(1 - t|z|)^{ \frac{\alpha+2}{p}+1}} \right)^p \frac{(1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha+1}}{|1 - \overline{b}z|^{2}} dA(z) \\
\lesssim& \| f \|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p \sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}} (1-|b|^2) \left( \int_0^1 \left( \int_{\mathbb{D}} \frac{(1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha+1} dA(z)}{|1 - tz|^p(1 - t|z|)^{p+\alpha+2}  |1 - \overline{b}z|^{2}} \right)^{\frac{1}{p}} d\mu(t) \right)^{p}.
\end{aligned}
\] 	
To complete the proof, it suffices to prove 
\[
\sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}} (1-|b|^2) \left( \int_0^1 \left( \int_{\mathbb{D}} \frac{(1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha+1} dA(z)}{|1 - tz|^p(1 - t|z|)^{p+\alpha+2}  |1 - \overline{b}z|^{2}} \right)^{\frac{1}{p}} d\mu(t) \right)^{p}< \infty.
\]

{\bf Case \( p > 1 \).}
Using the polar coordinate formula and Lemma \ref{le2.2} (i), we get
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\int_{\mathbb{D}} \frac{(1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha+1} }{|1 - tz|^p(1 - t|z|)^{p+\alpha+2}  |1 - \overline{b}z|^{2}}dA(z) \\
\asymp& \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1 - tr)^{p+\alpha+2}} \int_0^{2\pi} \frac{d\theta}{|1 - tre^{i\theta}|^p |1 - \overline{b}re^{i\theta}|^{2}} dr \\
\asymp& \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1 - tr)^{p+\alpha+2}} \left( \frac{1}{(1 - tr)^{p - 1} |1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^{2}} + \frac{1}{(1 - |b|r) |1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^p} \right) dr \\
=&\int_{0}^{1}\frac{(1-r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1-tr)^{2p+\alpha+1}|1-t\overline{b}r^2|^2}dr+\int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1 - tr)^{p+\alpha+2}(1-|b|r)|1-t\overline{b}r^2|^p}dr\\
=& J_1+J_2.
\end{aligned}
\] 
Using the fact that 
\begin{align}\label{xy}
(x + y)^p \leqslant 
\begin{cases} 
	x^p + y^p, & 0<p<1, \\
	2^{p-1}(x^p + y^p), & p \ge 1 
\end{cases}, \quad x,y>0,
\end{align}
we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}} (1-|b|^2) \left( \int_0^1 \left( \int_{\mathbb{D}} \frac{(1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha+1} dA(z)}{|1 - tz|^p(1 - t|z|)^{p+\alpha+2}  |1 - \overline{b}z|^{2}} \right)^{\frac{1}{p}} d\mu(t) \right)^{p}\\
\lesssim& \sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}} (1-|b|^2) \left(\int_0^1 (J_1 + J_2)^{\frac{1}{p}} d\mu(t)\right)^p \\
\lesssim& \sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}} (1-|b|^2) \left(\int_0^1 J_1^{\frac{1}{p}} d\mu(t)\right)^p + \sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}} (1-|b|^2) \left(\int_0^1 J_2^{\frac{1}{p}} d\mu(t)\right)^p.
\end{aligned}
\]
It is easy to see that \( 1 - r < 1 - tr \), \( 1 - t < 1 - tr \) and \(|1-t\overline{b}r^2|\ge 1-t|b|r\).
Therefore, we can choose a positive real number \( \epsilon \) that satisfies
 \[ \frac{p-1}{p}< \epsilon <1. \] 
                                                                                             
By the choice of \( \epsilon \), it is easy to check that \( p\epsilon-p> -1 \) and \( 2 - (p\epsilon-p) - 1 = 1-p\epsilon+p > 0 \). 
Using Lemma \ref{le2.3}, we get
\[
\begin{aligned}
J_1 &= \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1 - tr)^{2p+\alpha+1} |1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^{2}}dr \\
&\leq \int_0^1 \frac{1}{(1 - tr)^{p} |1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^{2}}dr \\
&\leq \int_0^1 \frac{1}{(1 - t)^{p\epsilon} (1 - tr)^{p-p\epsilon} |1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^{2}}dr \\
&\lesssim \frac{1}{(1 - t)^{p\epsilon}} \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p\epsilon-p}}{(1 - t|b|r)^{2}} dr\\
&\lesssim \frac{1}{(1 - t)^{p\epsilon} (1 - t|b|)^{1-p\epsilon+p}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $\mu$ is a Carleson measure, using Lemma \ref{le2.4}, we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}} (1-|b|^2) \left(\int_0^1 J_1^{\frac{1}{p}} d\mu(t) \right)^p\\
\lesssim &
\sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}} \left( \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - |b|)^{\frac{1}{p}}}{(1 - t)^{\epsilon} (1 - t|b|)^{\frac{1}{p}-\epsilon+1}} d\mu(t) \right)^p
\lesssim 1.
\end{aligned}
\]   
Subsequently, we focus our efforts on the estimation of \(J_2\). 


Let \( 0 < \delta <1\) 
and 
\( 0 < \tau < \frac{1}{p} \). We may choose \( \delta \) and \( \tau \) such that \( \frac{1}{p} < \delta + \tau < \frac{p+1}{p} \). Notice that \( 1 -r  < 1 - |b|r \) and \( 1 - |b| < 1 - |b|r \). By the choices of \( \delta \) and  \( \tau \), it is easy to see that \( p(\delta+\tau)-2> -1 \) and \( p-[p(\delta+\tau)-2]-1 = p-p(\delta+\tau)+1> 0 \). Using Lemma \ref{le2.3}, it follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
J_2 &= \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1 - tr)^{p+\alpha+2}(1 - |b|r)|1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^p} dr \\
&\leq \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1 - t)^{p\delta}(1 - tr)^{p+\alpha+2-p\delta}(1 - |b|)^{p\tau}(1 - |b|r)^{ 1- p\tau}|1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^p} dr \\
&\leq \frac{1}{(1 - t)^{p\delta}(1 - |b|)^{p\tau}} \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+3- p\delta- p\tau}|1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^p} dr \\
&\lesssim \frac{1}{(1 - t)^{p\delta}(1 - |b|)^{p\tau}} \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p(\delta+\tau)-2}}{(1 - t|b|r)^p} dr\\
&\lesssim \frac{1}{(1 - t)^{p\delta}(1 - |b|)^{p\tau}(1 - t|b|)^{p-p(\delta+\tau)+1}}.
\end{aligned}
\] 
Since \( \mu \) is a Carleson measure, using Lemma \ref{le2.4}, we get 
\[
\begin{aligned}
	&\sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}} (1-|b|^2) \left(\int_0^1 J_2^{\frac{1}{p}} d\mu(t) \right)^p\\
	\lesssim &
	\sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}} \left( \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - |b|)^{\frac{1}{p}-\tau}}{(1 - t)^{\delta} (1 - t|b|)^{1-(\delta+\tau)+\frac{1}{p}}} d\mu(t) \right)^p
	\lesssim 1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, 
\[
\| \mathcal{C}_\mu (f) \|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)} \lesssim \| f \|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}.\]
    
 
    
    
    
    
{\bf Case \( p =1 \).}
Using Lemma \ref{le2.2} (ii), we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1 - tr)^{p+\alpha+2}} \int_0^{2\pi} \frac{d\theta}{|1 - tre^{i\theta}|^p |1 - \overline{b}re^{i\theta}|^{2}} dr \\
\asymp& \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1 - tr)^{p+\alpha+2}}
\left( \frac{1}{(1-|b|r) |1 - t\overline{b}r^2|} +\frac{1}{|1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^2}\log \frac{e}{1 - |\varphi_{br}(tr)|^2} \right) dr\\
=& \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1 - tr)^{p+\alpha+2}(1-|b|r) |1 - t\overline{b}r^2|} dr + \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}  \log \frac{e}{1 - |\varphi_{br}(tr)|^2} }{(1 - tr)^{p+\alpha+2} |1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^2}dr \\
=&J_3 + J_4.
\end{aligned}
\]
The estimation of \(J_3\) follows the same procedure as that of \(J_1\) and we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}} (1-|b|^2) \left(\int_0^1 J_3^{\frac{1}{p}} d\mu(t) \right)^p 
\lesssim 1.
\end{aligned}
\]   

 Finally, we estimate \(J_4\).
Let \( 0 < d < \frac{1}{4} \). It is obvious that
\[
(1 - |\varphi_{br}(tr)|^2)^d \log \frac{e}{1 - |\varphi_{br}(tr)|^2} \lesssim 1.
\]
Since \( 2d + \frac{1}{2} < 1 \), we may choose a positive real number \( \gamma \) such that \( 2d + \frac{1}{2} < \gamma < 1 \). This yields that \(\gamma-1-2d > -1 \) and \( 2-2d - (\gamma-1-2d) - 1 =2-\gamma> 0 \). Bear in mind that \( 1 - t < 1 - tr \), \(1-r<1-tr\) and \( 1 - r < 1 - |b|r \). Using Lemma \ref{le2.3}, it follows that  
\[
\begin{aligned}
J_4 &= \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1} }{(1 - tr)^{p+\alpha+2} |1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^2}\log \frac{e}{1 - |\varphi_{br}(tr)|^2} dr \\
&\lesssim \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1 - tr)^{p+\alpha+2} |1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^2 (1 - |\varphi_{br}(tr)|^2)^d} dr \\
&= \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1 - tr)^{p+\alpha+2+d} (1 - |b|r)^d |1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^{2 - 2d}} dr\\
&\leq  \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - r)^{p+\alpha+1}}{(1-tr)^{p+\alpha+2+d-\gamma}(1 - t)^\gamma (1-r)^d |1 - t\overline{b}r^2|^{2 - 2d}} dr \\
&\le
\frac{1}{(1 - t)^\gamma}\int_0^1
\frac{(1 - r)^{\gamma-1-2d}}{(1 - t|b|r)^{2-2d}} dr\\
&\lesssim \frac{1}{(1 - t)^\gamma (1 - t|b|)^{2-\gamma}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \( \mu \) is a Carleson measure, using Lemma \ref{le2.4}  we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}} (1-|b|^2) \left(\int_0^1 J_4^{\frac{1}{p}} d\mu(t)\right)^p\\ 
\lesssim &
\sup_{b \in \mathbb{D}}\left( \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - |b|)^{\frac{1}{p}}}{(1 - t)^{\frac{\gamma}{p}} (1 - t|b|)^{1+\frac{1}{p}-\frac{\gamma}{p}}} d\mu(t)\right)^p  
\lesssim  1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence,
\[
\| \mathcal{C}_\mu (f) \|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)} \lesssim \| f \|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)},
\] 
which implies that \(\mathcal{C}_\mu\) is bounded on \(AT_p^\infty(\alpha)\). 
The proof is complete.

title: Theorem
body_md: Let \(1 \leq p<\infty\) and \(\alpha>-2\). Let \(\mu\) be a finite positive Borel measure on $[0, 1)$. The Ces\`aro-like operator \(\mathcal{C}_\mu\) is compact on \(AT_p^\infty(\alpha)\) if and only if \(\mu\) is a vanishing Carleson measure.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First we assume that \( \mathcal{C}_\mu \) is compact on \( AT_p^\infty(\alpha) \). For \( \frac{1}{2} < \rho < 1 \), let  
\[
f_\rho(z) = \frac{(1 - \rho)}{(1 - \rho z)^{ \frac{\alpha+2}{p}+1}}, \quad z \in \mathbb{D}.
\]  
We see that \( f_\rho \in AT_p^\infty(\alpha) \) and \( \sup_{\frac{1}{2} < \rho < 1} \| f_\rho \|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)} \lesssim 1 \). 
Furthermore,   \(f_\rho\to 0\) uniformly on compact subsets of \(\mathbb{D}\) as \(\rho\to 1\).
Since \( \mathcal{C}_\mu \) is compact on \( AT_p^\infty(\alpha) \), by virtue of  Lemma \ref{com}, it follows that  \[ \lim_{\rho \to 1} \| \mathcal{C}_\mu (f_\rho) \|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)} = 0  .\] 
Using Lemma \ref{az}, we have
\begin{align}\label{4.1}
\sup_{z \in \mathbb{D}} (1 - |z|^2)^{\frac{\alpha+2}{p}} |\mathcal{C}_\mu (f_\rho)(z)| \lesssim \| \mathcal{C}_\mu (f_\rho) \|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)} \to 0, \quad \text{as} \quad \rho \to 1. 
\end{align}
Thus, for \( \frac{1}{2}< \rho < 1 \),  by the proof of    Theorem \ref{cmub}  we have 
\[\begin{aligned} 
 (1-\rho)^{ \frac{\alpha+2}{p}}|\mathcal{C}_\mu (f_\rho)(\rho)|  \gtrsim  \frac{\mu([\rho, 1))}{1-\rho},
\end{aligned}\]
                   
                                                               
                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                   
                                        
                
which implies that  
\[
\frac{\mu([\rho, 1))}{1 - \rho} \lesssim \| \mathcal{C}_\mu (f_\rho) \|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}.
\]  
Combining with (\ref{4.1}), we get that \(\mu\) is a vanishing Carleson measure.
	

Conversely, suppose  \(\mu\) is a vanishing Carleson measure. Consider a bounded sequence \(\{f_j\}_{j=1}^\infty\) in \(AT_p^\infty(\alpha)\) that converges uniformly to 0 on every compact subset of \(\mathbb{D}\). We may assume without loss of generality that \(f_j(0) = 0\) for all \(j \geq 1\) and \(\sup_{j \geq 1} \|f_j\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)} \lesssim 1\). Using Lemma \ref{com}, we need to establish that
$$
\lim_{j \to \infty} \|C_\mu(f_j)\|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)} = 0.
$$	
Since \( \mu \) is a vanishing Carleson measure, for any \( \epsilon > 0 \), using Lemma \ref{le4.2}, we obtain that there exists a \(  \delta \in (0,1)  \) such that  
\[
\int_0^1 \frac{(1 - |b|)^r}{(1 - t)^c (1 - t|b|)^{1 + r - c}} d\mu(t) < \epsilon  \quad \text{ for all } \quad \delta < |b| < 1,
\]  
where \(r>0 \) and \( 0 \leq c < 1 \). 
Observe that Lemma \ref{le4.2} also indicates that \( \int_0^1 \frac{1}{(1 - t)^c} d\mu(t) < \infty \). As a result, there exists a $t_0$ with \( 0 < t_0 < 1 \) for which  
\begin{align}\label{4.2}
\int_{t_0}^1 \frac{1}{(1 - t)^c} d\mu(t) < \epsilon.
\end{align}
Using Lemma \ref{at}, we get
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \| \mathcal{C}_\mu (f_j) \|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)}^p  
\lesssim& \sup_{|b| \leq \delta}  \int_{\mathbb{D}} |\mathcal{C}_\mu (f_j)'(z)|^p (1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha} (1 - |\varphi_b(z)|^2) dA(z)\\
&+ \sup_{\delta < |b| < 1}  \int_{\mathbb{D}} |\mathcal{C}_\mu (f_j)'(z)|^p (1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha} (1 - |\varphi_b(z)|^2) dA(z) \\
=& H_1+H_2.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(H_2\), by Theorem \ref{cmub}, we obtain that
\[	
H_2 \lesssim \sup_{\delta < |b| < 1} \int_0^1 \frac{(1 - |b|)^r}{(1 - t)^c (1 - t|b|)^{1 + r - c}} d\mu(t) < \epsilon
\]
for some \(r>0 \) and \( 0 \leq c < 1 \).
Furthermore, using (\ref{xy}), we get
\[
\begin{aligned}
H_1 =&\sup_{|b| \leq \delta}  \int_{\mathbb{D}} |\mathcal{C}_\mu (f_j)'(z)|^p (1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha} (1 - |\varphi_b(z)|^2) dA(z)  \\
\leq& \sup_{|b| \leq \delta}  \int_{\mathbb{D}} \left( \int_0^1 \left( \frac{|f_j(tz)|}{|1 - tz|^2} + \frac{|f_j'(tz)|}{|1 - tz|} \right) d\mu(t) \right)^p (1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha} (1 - |\varphi_b(z)|^2) dA(z)  \\
\lesssim& \sup_{|b| \leq \delta}  \int_{\mathbb{D}} \left( \int_0^{t_0} \left( \frac{|f_j(tz)|}{|1 - tz|^2} + \frac{|f_j'(tz)|}{|1 - tz|} \right) d\mu(t) \right)^p (1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha} (1 - |\varphi_b(z)|^2) dA(z)  \\
&+ \sup_{|b| \leq \delta}  \int_{\mathbb{D}} \left( \int_{t_0}^1 \left( \frac{|f_j(tz)|}{|1 - tz|^2} + \frac{|f_j'(tz)|}{|1 - tz|} \right) d\mu(t) \right)^p (1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha} (1 - |\varphi_b(z)|^2) dA(z).
\end{aligned}
\] 
By virtue of the Cauchy integral theorem, it can be deduced that the sequence \(\{f_j'\}_{j = 1}^{\infty}\) converges uniformly to \(0\) on every compact subset of \(\mathbb{D}\). 
Hence,
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_{|b| \leq \delta}  \int_{\mathbb{D}} \left( \int_0^{t_0} \left( \frac{|f_j(tz)|}{|1 - tz|^2} + \frac{|f_j'(tz)|}{|1 - tz|} \right) d\mu(t) \right)^p (1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha} (1 - |\varphi_b(z)|^2) dA(z)  \\
\lesssim& \sup_{|w| \leq t_0} (|f_j(w)| + |f_j'(w)|) \to 0, \quad  j \to \infty.
\end{aligned}
\]
Similar to the proof of Theorem \ref{cmub}, we can also show that 
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_{|b| \leq \delta}  \int_{\mathbb{D}} \left( \int_{t_0}^1 \left( \frac{|f_j(tz)|}{|1 - tz|^2} + \frac{|f_j'(tz)|}{|1 - tz|} \right) d\mu(t) \right)^p (1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha} (1 - |\varphi_b(z)|^2) dA(z)  \\
\lesssim &\sup_{|b| \leq \delta} (1-|b|^2)  \int_{\mathbb{D}} \left( \int_{t_0}^1 \frac{d\mu(t)}{|1 - tz|(1 - t|z|)^{ \frac{\alpha+2}{p}+1} } \right)^p \frac{(1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha+1}}{|1 - \overline{b}z|^{2}} dA(z)  \\
\lesssim &\sup_{|b| \leq \delta} (1-|b|^2) \left( \int_{t_0}^1 \left( \int_{\mathbb{D}} \frac{(1 - |z|^2)^{p+\alpha+1} dA(z)}{|1 - tz|^p(1 - t|z|)^{p+\alpha+2}  |1 - \overline{b}z|^{2}} \right)^{\frac{1}{p}} d\mu(t) \right)^p\\
\lesssim& \sup_{|b| \leq \delta}\left( \int_{t_0}^1 \frac{(1 - |b|)^r}{(1 - t)^c (1 - t|b|)^{1 + r- c}} d\mu(t) \right)^p
\end{aligned}
\]
for some \(r>0 \) and \( 0 \leq c < 1 \). By (\ref{4.2}), we deduce that
\[
\sup_{|b| \leq \delta} \int_{t_0}^1 \frac{(1 - |b|)^r}{(1 - t)^c (1 - t|b|)^{1 + r - c}} d\mu(t) \lesssim \int_{t_0}^1 \frac{1}{(1 - t)^c} d\mu(t) < \epsilon.
\] 
Therefore,  
\[
\lim_{j \to \infty} \| \mathcal{C}_\mu (f_j) \|_{AT_p^\infty(\alpha)} = 0.
\]  
The proof is complete.
